raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes item 7 of #61608. With `--enable-tower-connector-lora`, LLaVA-NeXT-Video's `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` counts 576 tower rows per frame, but vLLM's CLIP tower prepends a CLS token, so its LoRA layers actually see 577. The tower LoRA buffer is sized from this count, so encoder profiling overflows it and the engine fails to start:

```
$ vllm serve llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf --enable-lora --enable-tower-connector-lora
...
  File "vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py", line 291, in _lora_shrink
    assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M
AssertionError
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

When startup does pass (e.g. `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`), the runtime mapping is still one row per frame short, so the last rows of each video get the next request's adapter, or none.

The fix adds `tower_tokens_per_frame` in `__init__`, computed with `get_num_image_tokens()` as in `llava_next.py` (577 for CLIP, unchanged for SigLIP), and the hook uses it instead of `patch_grid_length ** 2`. #61799 fixes the same bug in `llava.py`; no open PR touches these counts in `llava_next_video.py`.

## Validation

1x A100 80GB, base 5bf3d9f665, `llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf`:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm serve` command above (defaults otherwise) | assert at startup | starts |
| `LLM(...)`, `max_model_len=4096`, `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048 / 8192 | assert at startup | starts |
| `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` (default `max_model_len`), 70-frame + 43-frame video in one batch | assert at runtime | completes |
| no-LoRA requests in a batch with LoRA requests vs. the same batch without LoRA | one request's logprobs change | bit-exact |
| tower LoRA vs. the same adapter merged into the weights, max \|Δlogprob\| | 0.039 | 0.012 |

The last two rows use a random rank-8 adapter on the CLIP layers, with 4 eight-frame videos in one encoder batch and greedy decoding.

All GPU runs above used the first revision (fd4daa1), which computed the same count inside the hook; the review update only moves it to `__init__`.

`pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_llava_next_video.py`: 6 passed on e40576d.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

The fix looks reasonable to me. However, I think we could keep the existing initialization logic and simply add `tower_tokens_per_frame` using `get_num_image_tokens()`. This would also avoid the need to refactor the existing tests so extensively.
